title: Sprint 4 — Hangfire, MailKit, QuestPDF, File Security & Serilog
summary: Offload heavy operations from the request: Hangfire, QuestPDF receipts, MailKit emails, secure file uploads, and Serilog.

briefBlocks.text: Sprint 4 — Hangfire, MailKit, QuestPDF, File Security & Serilog

briefBlocks.markdown: We continue building **DonationHub** — the Donation Management & Crowdfunding Platform. Now that Sprint 3 gave us the donation success flow inside a single transaction, it is time to move every **heavy or slow** operation out of the HTTP request pipeline: generating PDF receipts, sending emails, and running delayed and recurring jobs. In the same sprint, we secure campaign banner uploads and configure Structured Logging covering both HTTP requests and background jobs.
- **Evaluation:** 100 Points
**Target Framework:** .NET 10 (`net10.0`) with the `.slnx` solution format, fully compatible with .NET 8 and .NET 9.

Eliminate heavy, blocking operations from the HTTP request pipeline. When a donation completes, offload receipt generation and email notifications to background workers using **Hangfire**. Generate professional PDF receipts using **QuestPDF**, send transactional emails via **MailKit** tested locally against a **Mailpit** container, enforce security on campaign file uploads via **Magic Bytes verification**, schedule delayed and recurring maintenance jobs, and configure structured logging using **Serilog** (Console + rolling file; **Seq** is an optional BONUS sink).

briefBlocks.code:
HTTP Donation Completed (success flow transaction)
           ↓
Transaction Commits
           ↓
Enqueue Hangfire Job (Fire-and-Forget) — only AFTER the commit
           ↓
Immediate HTTP 200 OK Returned to Client
           ↓ (Background Worker)
Generate PDF Receipt via QuestPDF
           ↓
Send Email with Attachment via MailKit (Captured in Mailpit)

briefBlocks.markdown: Notice the order: the job is **enqueued only AFTER** the commit succeeds, and the client receives `200 OK` immediately without waiting for PDF generation or SMTP.

briefBlocks.text: Local SMTP Testing via Mailpit in Docker

briefBlocks.markdown: *To test email delivery locally without leaking test emails to real inboxes, run a local Mailpit container:*

- SMTP Server runs on `localhost:1025` (no TLS in development).
- Web Dashboard is accessible at `http://localhost:8025` to inspect rendered emails as recipients will see them, along with their attachments.

# Later: start the existing container instead of creating a new one
docker start mailpit
docker ps --filter name=mailpit

briefBlocks.markdown: Mailpit captures **all** emails regardless of the recipient address, so you can safely use fake email addresses for seed accounts.

| Package / Tool | License / Configuration | Notes & Rules |
|---|---|---|
| **QuestPDF** | Community License | `QuestPDF.Settings.License = LicenseType.Community;` in `Program.cs`. Free for individuals, small businesses, education, and open-source projects. |
| **Hangfire** | LGPL v3 Free Core | Use `Hangfire.Core`, `Hangfire.AspNetCore`, and `Hangfire.SqlServer`. Avoid paid commercial Pro extensions. |
| **Mailpit** | MIT | Container `axllent/mailpit` for zero-risk local email interception. |
| **Serilog** | Apache 2.0 | CORE sinks: Console + rolling file. Structured logging enriched with `traceId` and the user id (when authenticated). |
| **Seq** *(BONUS)* | Free developer instance | Optional extra Serilog sink. Not required for CORE. |
| **Secrets** | User secrets / environment variables | SMTP credentials and `HangfireDashboardOptions` credentials must **never** be committed in `appsettings*.json`. |

**Secrets always stay out of Git:** SMTP credentials and the Hangfire dashboard username/password are read from `dotnet user-secrets` in development and from environment variables elsewhere. Once committed, they remain in repository history even if you delete them later.
Hangfire automatically creates its tables in the same SQL Server database under a separate schema named `HangFire`; these tables are **not** part of your EF Core Migrations.
All tasks below are **CORE** unless marked BONUS.

Links marked with 📘 are from the free [.NET Web API Zero to Hero](https://codewithmukesh.com/courses/dotnet-webapi-zero-to-hero/) course (.NET 10 articles with full source code). Its examples use **PostgreSQL** and **Minimal APIs** — apply the same concepts using **SQL Server** and **thin Controllers** as in our project, and stick to the package versions installed in the solution.
Implement background job orchestration according to SRS §5.8:

items: Configure Hangfire with SQL Server persistent storage: `UseSqlServerStorage`.
Register the Hangfire server in `Program.cs`: `builder.Services.AddHangfireServer()`.
**JOB-05 (Protected Dashboard):** Protect the Hangfire dashboard endpoint `/hangfire` and do not leave it open to the public.

A browser cannot send a JWT, so use **basic authentication** with credentials bound from `HangfireDashboardOptions` (validated with `ValidateOnStart()`, values from user secrets / environment variables). An ASP.NET Core policy requiring the `Admin` role is also an acceptable alternative.
**Retries (NTF-04):** Every job retries automatically **at least 3 times** (e.g., `[AutomaticRetry(Attempts = 3)]` or a global filter), and each failure is logged at `Error` level.

briefBlocks.markdown: Hangfire's default dashboard configuration only allows local requests (`LocalRequestsOnlyAuthorizationFilter`), which is **not real protection**: behind a reverse proxy or inside Docker, all requests can appear "local". Write your own authorization filter (basic auth), or use the acceptable alternative: a policy requiring the `Admin` role.
Basic authentication only sends credentials Base64-encoded (not real encryption), so always use it over **HTTPS**.

briefBlocks.text: Task 2 — Transactional Email Service via MailKit & Mailpit

briefBlocks.markdown: Implement the notifications module according to SRS §5.6:

items: **NTF-01:** Define `IEmailService` in `DonationHub.Application` and implement it in `DonationHub.Infrastructure` using **MailKit** and **MimeKit**, with SMTP settings from `EmailOptions` (Host, Port, SenderEmail, SenderName; credentials from user secrets / environment variables).
**NTF-02:** Email the receipt to the donor after a successful donation, with the PDF receipt attached (sent by JOB-01).
**NTF-03:** Email the campaign creator when the campaign reaches its goal (sent by JOB-02).
**NTF-04:** Emails are sent **only by Hangfire jobs, never inside the HTTP request**. A failed job retries (at least 3 attempts) and logs the failure.
**NTF-05:** Email text uses the recipient's `PreferredLanguage` (`ar` or `en`). Arabic emails render right-to-left (`<html dir="rtl" lang="ar">`).
**NTF-06:** In Development, emails go to the local Mailpit container (`localhost:1025`); no real email is sent.
Send HTML-formatted transactional emails with optional attachments.

briefBlocks.markdown: `IEmailService` is a small interface that knows nothing about MailKit: Application knows "send an email", and Infrastructure knows "how". This simplifies testing and lets you swap email providers later without touching business logic.

briefBlocks.text: Task 3 — Dynamic PDF Receipt Generation via QuestPDF

briefBlocks.markdown: Implement donor receipt generation according to SRS §5.7 (FIL-06, FIL-07):

items: Configure QuestPDF with Community license: `QuestPDF.Settings.License = LicenseType.Community;`.
**FIL-06:** Generate a PDF receipt for each succeeded donation **inside a Hangfire job** (never in the request).
Generate the receipt as a byte array / stream and store it through `IFileStorage` so it can be downloaded later.
**FIL-07:** `GET /donations/{id}/receipt` downloads the PDF (`application/pdf`), **only for the donation owner or an Admin**. Another user's donation returns 404.

briefBlocks.markdown:
The receipt contains, in the **donor's `PreferredLanguage`**:

- Receipt Number (`DN-{year}-{6-digit sequence}`, generated in the success flow) and Transaction Date.
- Campaign Title (in the donor's language) and Category.
- Donor Name. *(BONUS only, if DON-11 is implemented: show "Anonymous Donor" when `IsAnonymous = true`.)*
- Formatted Amount and Currency.
- Organization verification header and footer.

briefBlocks.code:
// Program.cs — before generating any document
QuestPDF.Settings.License = LicenseType.Community;

briefBlocks.markdown:
| Method | Path | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/donations/{id}/receipt` | Owner, Admin |
PDF receipts contain personal data: **never store them in a publicly served folder** (such as `wwwroot`). Downloads must pass solely through the protected endpoint that verifies ownership.
Arabic text in a PDF requires a font that supports Arabic glyphs, and the page requires right-to-left direction. Test an Arabic receipt early and do not wait until the last day.

briefBlocks.text: Task 4 — Secure File Uploads & Magic Bytes Validation

briefBlocks.markdown: Implement campaign banner uploads according to SRS §5.7:

items: **FIL-01:** Upload a campaign banner via `IFormFile` (`multipart/form-data`). Allowed only for an **Admin or the campaign's owner** (Campaign Manager). Allowed types: JPG, PNG, WEBP. Max size **2 MB**, configurable via `FileStorageOptions`.

**FIL-02 — Security Invariant (Magic Bytes):** Do not rely on file extension or client `ContentType` headers (these can be easily spoofed). Validate file headers by inspecting the initial raw binary signatures (Magic Bytes) to verify legitimate JPEG, PNG, or WebP files.

**FIL-03:** Store files through an `IFileStorage` abstraction (defined in Application, local disk implementation in Infrastructure). Save under a generated random name (`Guid`), never the user's file name.
**FIL-04:** Replacing a banner deletes the old file. Soft-deleting a campaign keeps the file (hard cleanup not required).
**FIL-05:** The banner is served publicly through a URL returned in the campaign response (e.g., `bannerUrl`).
**Errors:** wrong type or failed signature check → `File.InvalidType` (400); file over the limit → `File.TooLarge` (413).

briefBlocks.markdown:
| Method | Path | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/campaigns/{id}/banner` | Admin, or owner Campaign Manager (multipart/form-data) |
| `DELETE` | `/campaigns/{id}/banner` | Admin, or owner Campaign Manager |

**Required File Signatures (for reference):**

| Type | Leading Bytes (Hex) |
|---|---|
| JPEG | `FF D8 FF` |
| PNG | `89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A` |
| WebP | `52 49 46 46` ("RIFF"), then 4 size bytes, then `57 45 42 50` ("WEBP") |
Critical acceptance test: rename an `.exe` file to `.jpg` and upload it — it must be rejected with `File.InvalidType` (400). An `.exe` file starts with the two bytes `4D 5A` ("MZ").
Apply the ownership rule just as in Sprint 3: a Campaign Manager attempting to modify the banner of a campaign they do not own receives 404 (never reveal the existence of other users' resources).

briefBlocks.text: Task 5 — Asynchronous Jobs: Donation Processing & Expired Campaigns

briefBlocks.markdown: Implement the jobs according to SRS §5.8 and the success flow in SRS §5.5:

items: **Enqueue after commit:** Jobs are enqueued **only AFTER the success-flow transaction commits**, never inside the transaction.
The temporary stub `POST /admin/donations/{id}/mark-succeeded` (Admin, DON-06) is still present in this sprint and triggers the same flow.
**JOB-01 (Fire-and-forget) — Send donation receipt:** after a donation succeeds, the job fetches the donation, generates the PDF receipt (FIL-06), and emails it to the donor (NTF-02).
**JOB-02 (Fire-and-forget) — Send goal-reached email:** if the campaign just became `Completed`, enqueue a job to email the campaign creator (NTF-03).

**JOB-03 (Delayed) — Fail stale pending donation (DON-09):** when a donation is created (`POST /campaigns/{campaignId}/donations`), schedule `BackgroundJob.Schedule(...)` to run after `DonationOptions.PendingTimeoutMinutes` (default **30 minutes**). If the donation is still `Pending`, it becomes `Failed`; otherwise the job does nothing.
**JOB-04 (Recurring, hourly):** Register a **Recurring Job** running every hour (`Cron.Hourly()` / `0 * * * *`) that marks all `Active` campaigns past their `EndDate` as `Expired`.

**Idempotency:** Jobs must be idempotent — running a job twice must not send two emails or change state twice (e.g., check a `ReceiptSentAt` / `GoalEmailSentAt` marker or the current status before acting).
**Hangfire Best Practice:** Pass only entity IDs (`Guid`/`int`) as job arguments, never full entities or `DbContext` instances.
Donation amounts remain validated against `DonationOptions` (min 1.00, max 10,000.00).

briefBlocks.markdown: Required enqueue example for JOB-01 (as specified):

| ID | Job | Type | Behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| JOB-01 | Send donation receipt | Fire-and-forget | Generate PDF then email it |
| JOB-02 | Send goal-reached email | Fire-and-forget | To the campaign creator |
| JOB-03 | Fail stale pending donation | Delayed | Scheduled when a donation is created, runs after the pending timeout, fails the donation if it is still `Pending` |
| JOB-04 | Expire campaigns | Recurring (hourly) | `Active` campaigns past `EndDate` become `Expired` |
| JOB-05 | Hangfire dashboard | — | Enabled and protected (not publicly open) |

**Why after the commit?** If you enqueue the job before the commit and the transaction rolls back, the worker would email a receipt for a donation that never succeeded. And if the worker picks up the job before the commit completes, it may not see the new data yet.
Ask yourself for every job: "What happens if it runs twice?" and "What if it fails halfway through and retries?". This is exactly the kind of question asked in the explanation part of the evaluation.

briefBlocks.text: Task 6 — Structured Logging with Serilog (Seq optional)

briefBlocks.markdown: Implement logging according to SRS §6.10:

items: Replace the default logger with Serilog (`Serilog.AspNetCore`).
**CORE sinks:** Console and **rolling file** (e.g., `logs/donationhub-.log`, rolling daily). *A **Seq** sink (local or containerized) is a BONUS.*
Enable request logging middleware (`UseSerilogRequestLogging`) capturing status code and duration.
Enrich every log entry with the correlation id (`traceId`) and the user id when authenticated.
Use structured message templates (`"Donation {DonationId} succeeded"`), not string concatenation.
Log levels: `Information` for business events, `Warning` for recoverable anomalies (e.g., late payment), `Error` for failures (including failed job attempts).
Never log secrets: passwords, JWT / refresh tokens, SMTP credentials, or card data.

briefBlocks.markdown: The difference between `$"Donation {id} succeeded"` and `"Donation {DonationId} succeeded"` is fundamental: the first produces a flat string, whereas the second stores `DonationId` as a first-class property you can search and filter by later.

solutionBlocks.markdown: This is a reference solution continuing the same codebase from previous sprints (`Entity`, `Campaign`, `Donation`, `Result`, `IUnitOfWork`, `IReadDbContext`...). The core idea of this sprint: **an HTTP request only mutates and persists state, while all slow or fallible work (PDF, SMTP, maintenance) runs in the background**, with jobs that tolerate retries without duplicate side effects.

To keep length manageable, some classes are shown as excerpts (such as `CreateDonationCommandHandler` from Sprint 3, and the Sprints 1–3 sections of `Program.cs`). Shared names follow the Sprint 2–3 definitions: `Result`/`Result<T>` and `Error` in `DonationHub.Domain.Common` (with `Result<T>.Success(value)`, `Result<T>.Failure(error)`, and implicit conversions), `ApiControllerBase.ProblemFrom(error)` and `FromResult(...)`, `ICurrentUser`, `ICampaignAuthorizer`, `ICacheService`, `IReceiptNumberGenerator.NextAsync(utcNow, ct)`, and `DonationOptions` in `Application/Common/Options`. If the names differ in your project, adapt them accordingly. The key parts for this sprint (filters, jobs, storage, signature validation, QuestPDF, MailKit, Serilog) are shown in full.

solutionBlocks.text: Task 1 — Hangfire: Storage, Retries, and Dashboard Protection

solutionBlocks.markdown: We use the same SQL Server database for Hangfire storage so we do not add new infrastructure; jobs remain persisted even if the app restarts (unlike `Task.Run` or an in-memory queue). Free packages only:

solutionBlocks.code:
dotnet add src/DonationHub.Infrastructure package Hangfire.Core
dotnet add src/DonationHub.Infrastructure package Hangfire.AspNetCore
dotnet add src/DonationHub.Infrastructure package Hangfire.SqlServer
dotnet add src/DonationHub.Infrastructure package MailKit
dotnet add src/DonationHub.Infrastructure package QuestPDF
dotnet add src/DonationHub.Api package Serilog.AspNetCore
dotnet add tests/DonationHub.UnitTests package Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing

solutionBlocks.markdown: The new configuration classes follow the same Sprint 1 pattern: Data Annotations + `ValidateOnStart()` so the application fails fast on startup if the dashboard password or sender address is missing. `FileStorageOptions` lives in Application because the upload handler needs the maximum file size:

Register all sprint services in a single extension method inside Infrastructure. Notice that retries and failure logging are **global filters** applied to every job, instead of relying on remembering to place an attribute on every method:

Hangfire adds a global `AutomaticRetry` filter with 10 attempts by default. Adding `AutomaticRetryAttribute { Attempts = 3 }` as a global filter (the documented Hangfire pattern) makes the last configuration take effect because the filter does not allow duplicates. **Verify it yourself:** make a job throw an exception and watch in the dashboard as it is scheduled for 3 retries before moving to `Failed`.
A server filter logs the start and end of each job, and logs every failed attempt at `Error` level — satisfying the "every failure is logged" rule once for all current and future jobs:

**Dashboard Protection (JOB-05):** A browser does not send a JWT when navigating to `/hangfire`, so we use basic auth. The filter returns `false` with a `WWW-Authenticate` header, prompting the browser to display the login dialog (Hangfire sets 401 itself). Comparison is performed on fixed-length hashes using `FixedTimeEquals` to prevent timing attacks:

Passing `Authorization` **replaces** the default `LocalRequestsOnlyAuthorizationFilter` — which is what we want. Remember, however, that basic auth without HTTPS sends the password essentially in the clear; keep `UseHttpsRedirection()` enabled.

solutionBlocks.code:
cd src/DonationHub.Api
dotnet user-secrets set "HangfireDashboard:Username" "jobs-admin"
dotnet user-secrets set "HangfireDashboard:Password" "<long random password>"
# In production: HangfireDashboard__Username and HangfireDashboard__Password as environment variables

solutionBlocks.markdown: **Acceptable alternative:** a policy requiring the `Admin` role. Note, however, that it requires browser-compatible authentication (cookie); with JWT alone, the browser will always get 401. That is why basic auth is the simplest option for a pure API project.

solutionBlocks.text: Task 2 — IEmailService with MailKit and Mailpit

solutionBlocks.markdown: Application defines a small contract that knows nothing about MailKit. We pass attachments as `byte[]` because the receipt is small (a few KB), which makes the email message easy to test:

Do not catch and swallow the exception inside `SendAsync`! If SMTP fails, **the exception must propagate to Hangfire** so the job retries and the failure is logged. Swallowing the error means the job "succeeds" while the donor receives nothing.

**NTF-05:** Templates follow `PreferredLanguage`, with Arabic using `dir="rtl"`. We use `ar-EG` for formatting (Gregorian calendar) and encode every user-supplied value with `HtmlEncode` to prevent HTML injection in emails:

**NTF-06:** The configuration above lives in `appsettings.Development.json` only, making it impossible for Development to send real emails. In production, `Email__Host`, `Email__Username`, and `Email__Password` are configured as environment variables. Open `http://localhost:8025` after testing a donation and verify that the attachment `DN-2026-000001.pdf` is present and the Arabic email renders right-to-left.

solutionBlocks.text: Task 3 — QuestPDF Receipt and Protected Download

solutionBlocks.markdown: The generator has no knowledge of the database: it receives a prepared `ReceiptData` (in the donor's language) and returns `byte[]`. This separates "what is written" from "how it is rendered" and keeps the generator safe as a Singleton:

**Arabic font:** The default font lacks Arabic glyphs, which produces empty boxes (tofu). Include a font file (such as `NotoNaskhArabic-Regular.ttf` under the OFL license) in the project with `CopyToOutputDirectory`, and register it once at startup: `FontManager.RegisterFont(File.OpenRead(Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, "Fonts", "NotoNaskhArabic-Regular.ttf")));`. **Verify** that the family name passed to `FontFamily(...)` matches the registered font name, and that numbers and Latin text (the receipt number) render properly.

**Calendar pitfall:** The neutral `ar` culture is treated like `ar-SA`, whose default calendar is **Hijri (Um Al-Qura)**, causing the transaction date to appear in an unexpected Hijri date. That is why we use `ar-EG` (Gregorian). The same note applies to emails.
**FIL-07:** Downloading is a standard read query. The ownership check lives **inside the query itself**, so another user's donation appears as "not found" (404) without revealing its existence:

**Design decision:** A receipt not yet generated (the job is still queued) returns `409 Donation.ReceiptNotReady` here instead of 404, because the donation actually exists but its state is not ready yet. Either choice is acceptable as long as you document it in the README and test it.

The golden rule: **both the extension and `ContentType` come from the client, meaning they can be completely spoofed**. The only thing we trust is the file content itself. We place the signature validator in Application as a pure function with zero I/O, making it a one-liner to unit test:

Notice that the saved extension comes from the **inspection result**, not from the uploaded file name. A file named `cat.png` containing JPEG bytes is stored as `.jpg` — so the server serves it with the right `Content-Type`.
We add two small methods to the `Campaign` entity so mutating `BannerFileName` stays encapsulated inside the entity (private setters as in Sprint 1):

The handler: ownership first (via `ICampaignAuthorizer` from Sprint 3, no new manual check), then size, then signature, then persistence. Notice the file order: we save the new file, then save to the database, and **only after that succeeds** do we delete the old file (FIL-04). If saving fails, we delete the new file and leave the old one intact:

Why is `RequestSizeLimit` larger than 2MB? If a request exceeds Kestrel's limit, it gets rejected before reaching the handler with a generic message rather than `File.TooLarge` in our uniform format. A higher ceiling protects the server from massive payloads while letting the handler return the proper error (413) for everything in between. Deletion (`DeleteCampaignBannerCommand(Guid CampaignId)`) uses the same ownership check (`ICampaignAuthorizer`): it calls `RemoveBanner` and saves, then **only after saving succeeds** deletes the file and invalidates the cache — the same order as uploading.
**FIL-05:** Only the banners folder is served as static files, while receipts remain outside any public path. We also add `nosniff` so browsers do not try to "sniff" the content type:
In the campaign response, we project `BannerFileName` and then map it to a URL after execution (keeping the SQL query clean):

**Don't forget the cache from Sprint 3:** this is why the handler calls `cache.InvalidateCampaignAsync(campaign.Id, ct)` after saving succeeds (and on deletion as well), invalidating the campaign and campaign-list keys in Redis — otherwise the old `bannerUrl`, whose file was just deleted, would keep appearing. Also add `storage/` to `.gitignore`.

solutionBlocks.text: Task 5 — Jobs: Post-Commit, IDs Only, and Idempotent

solutionBlocks.markdown: **Domain additions:** To make a job safely retryable, we need a durable "memory" of what has already been completed. We add small timestamp markers to the entities (with a migration). Each marker is set only once, so the entity itself guards against duplication:

solutionBlocks.code:
dotnet ef migrations add Sprint4_ReceiptsAndNotifications --project src/DonationHub.Infrastructure --startup-project src/DonationHub.Api
dotnet ef database update --project src/DonationHub.Infrastructure --startup-project src/DonationHub.Api

solutionBlocks.markdown: **Abstractions in Application:** Handlers know nothing about Hangfire. They simply say "schedule sending the receipt for this donation", which makes unit-testing handlers with Moq possible without a Hangfire server:

**Why `CancellationToken.None`?** Expression trees do not allow omitting optional arguments (error CS0854), so we pass it explicitly. Hangfire automatically replaces `CancellationToken.None` with a real token that cancels on server shutdown — so the job stops gracefully and is retried later.

**Success Flow (DON-07) — The only change to `DonationSuccessFlow` from Sprint 3:** we save first, then schedule. We determine "campaign **just** completed" by comparing the status before and after, so we do not send the goal-reached email on every late payment for an already completed campaign. Scheduling happens right after a successful `SaveChangesAsync` inside the same retry loop, so an attempt that fails with a `RowVersion` conflict schedules nothing. Because the constructor changed, update the Sprint 3 `DonationSuccessFlow` test to pass a `Mock<IBackgroundJobScheduler>`:

**Trade-off:** If the commit succeeds and the app crashes right before `Enqueue`, the receipt is lost. This is acceptable in this sprint, though you must be aware of it. The complete solution is the **Transactional Outbox** pattern: you write a "message" row to a table inside the same transaction, and a background job forwards it to Hangfire (see the enrichment video). Never "fix" this by putting `Enqueue` **before** the commit — that is worse, as it may send a receipt for a donation that was never saved.

**JOB-03 (DON-09):** When creating a donation, immediately after saving. The timeout is `DonationOptions.PendingTimeoutMinutes` (default 30), which has existed since Sprint 1, so we do not add a new setting. The handler takes an extra `IBackgroundJobScheduler jobs` parameter in its constructor (update the Sprint 3 test with a mock for it):

The job logic itself is a regular command in Application — fully testable. A donation that no longer exists or is no longer `Pending` is not an error, but a **normal state** (it was paid or failed before the timeout), so it returns success with no changes:

**A race condition to think about:** What if `mark-succeeded` arrives at the exact moment the job runs? Both read `Pending`, and one writes `Succeeded` while the other writes `Failed`. Solution: add `RowVersion` (concurrency token) to `Donation` just as you did on `Campaign` in DON-08; the second write fails with `DbUpdateConcurrencyException`, and the job retries, sees the terminal state, and does nothing.

**JOB-01 and JOB-02:** The notification service lives in Infrastructure because it combines Identity data (email, `PreferredLanguage`) with storage, PDF generation, and SMTP. Notice the **two persisted steps**: the PDF is generated and saved once (`ReceiptFileName`), and the email is marked after sending (`ReceiptSentAt`). Retrying after an SMTP failure will not regenerate a new file:

**"Exactly-once" is impossible with SMTP:** if the email is sent and the database connection drops before saving `ReceiptSentAt`, a retry will send a second email. What we guarantee is **at-least-once with a very narrow duplicate window**, and running the job again after it succeeds sends nothing. This is a great answer to "what if the job runs twice?". To prevent two concurrent executions for the same donation, you can add `[DisableConcurrentExecution]` (noting that it is a Hangfire attribute).

**JOB-04:** The recurring job goes through the Domain method `MarkExpiredIfDue` (not `ExecuteUpdate`, which bypasses invariants and `RowVersion`), and processes in batches so it does not load thousands of campaigns into memory. The query itself makes it idempotent: the second run finds no expired `Active` campaigns:

solutionBlocks.code:
// Program.cs — after app.Build(). AddOrUpdate with the same id will not duplicate the job on each startup
app.Services.GetRequiredService<IRecurringJobManager>()
    .AddOrUpdate<ExpireCampaignsJob>(
        "expire-campaigns",
        job => job.RunAsync(CancellationToken.None),
        Cron.Hourly());                       // 0 * * * *

solutionBlocks.markdown: After expiring campaigns, invalidate the campaign-list cache (Sprint 3); otherwise `Expired` campaigns will appear as `Active` until the cache expires. You can trigger the job manually from the dashboard (Recurring Jobs → Trigger now) to test it without waiting an hour.

solutionBlocks.text: Task 6 — Serilog: Structured Logging from Line One

solutionBlocks.markdown: We use the **bootstrap logger** pattern: a temporary logger catches startup errors (such as `ValidateOnStart` failures), then gets replaced by the full logger read from configuration. Here is `Program.cs` after this sprint (Sprints 1–3 sections abbreviated with comments):

The "request completed" log line is enriched via `EnrichDiagnosticContext`, whereas **all** other logs during the request (handlers, EF, etc.) need a middleware that pushes the properties into `LogContext` after authentication:

Use the same `traceId` source that appears in ProblemDetails (Sprint 2). When a user sends you an error response containing a `traceId`, searching the log file by it reveals everything that happened during that exact request.

All configuration lives in `appsettings.json` (no secrets here). The file uses compact JSON (CLEF) so tools can query it easily, and the Console uses a human-readable template displaying the properties:

Remove the old `"Logging"` section from `appsettings*.json` as it is no longer used. The `Serilog.AspNetCore` package brings in `Serilog.Sinks.Console`, `Serilog.Sinks.File`, `Serilog.Settings.Configuration`, and `Serilog.Formatting.Compact`; if any is missing in your project, reference it explicitly. Add `logs/` to `.gitignore`.
**Structured templates and log levels** — the difference shows when querying logs later:
Be careful with `{@Object}` (destructuring): logging an entire options or request object could inadvertently leak an SMTP password or refresh token. Log only specific safe properties.

solutionBlocks.code:
# DonationHub API — Sprint 4

## What was added
- Hangfire (SQL Server storage) with a basic-auth protected dashboard at /hangfire (JOB-05)
- Receipt PDF (QuestPDF, Community license) generated in a background job, downloadable via
  GET /api/v1/donations/{id}/receipt (owner or Admin)
- Receipt and goal-reached emails via MailKit, localized by PreferredLanguage (Arabic is RTL)
- Campaign banner upload/delete with magic-bytes validation (JPG/PNG/WEBP, max 2 MB)
- Jobs: stale pending donation (delayed, 30 min), expire campaigns (hourly)
- Serilog: console + rolling file (logs/donationhub-.log) enriched with TraceId and UserId

## Run locally
    docker run -d --name mailpit -p 8025:8025 -p 1025:1025 axllent/mailpit
    cd src/DonationHub.Api
    dotnet user-secrets set "HangfireDashboard:Username" "jobs-admin"
    dotnet user-secrets set "HangfireDashboard:Password" "<long random password>"
    cd ../..
    dotnet ef database update --project src/DonationHub.Infrastructure --startup-project src/DonationHub.Api
    dotnet run --project src/DonationHub.Api

## Try it
1. Create a donation, then call POST /api/v1/admin/donations/{id}/mark-succeeded as Admin.
2. Open http://localhost:8025 and check the email with the PDF receipt attached.
3. Open /hangfire (browser asks for the dashboard credentials) to see the processed jobs.
4. Upload an .exe renamed to .jpg to POST /api/v1/campaigns/{id}/banner and expect 400 File.InvalidType.

## Decisions
- Jobs are enqueued only after the transaction commits and receive IDs only.
- Idempotency markers: Donation.ReceiptFileName, Donation.ReceiptSentAt, Campaign.GoalEmailSentAt.
- Email delivery is at-least-once (SMTP cannot be exactly-once); a successful job never resends.
- Receipts are stored outside any public folder; only banners are served as static files.
- Receipt not generated yet returns 409 Donation.ReceiptNotReady.
- Known trade-off: a crash between commit and enqueue loses the job (Outbox pattern would fix it).

items: Sending email or generating PDF directly inside the controller or handler (even via `Task.Run`) instead of Hangfire.
Calling `Enqueue` before `SaveChangesAsync` / the commit, or inside the transaction.
Passing a full `Donation` entity or `DbContext` as a job argument instead of `Guid`.
Non-idempotent job: a retry sends a second email or generates a new PDF every time.
Swallowing an SMTP exception inside `try/catch`, making the job appear to succeed and preventing retries.
Leaving the `/hangfire` dashboard open, protecting it with `LocalRequestsOnly` only, or putting its password in `appsettings.json`.
Checking file type solely via `Path.GetExtension` or `file.ContentType`.
Saving files under the user's file name (`file.FileName`) or storing receipts inside `wwwroot`.
Deleting the old banner **before** the database save succeeds, or never deleting it at all.
The receipt endpoint returning 403 instead of 404 for another user's donation, or not checking ownership at all.
Logging messages using string interpolation (`$"..."`) instead of structured templates, or logging passwords/tokens.
Using `DateTime.UtcNow` inside jobs or handlers instead of `TimeProvider`.
Sending the goal-reached email on every late payment because the condition checks `Status == Completed` instead of "just completed".
Forgetting to invalidate the cache after changing a banner or expiring campaigns.

solutionBlocks.text: Questions to Prepare For in Code Review

items: What happens if the receipt job runs twice? And what if SMTP fails after generating the PDF?
Why do we enqueue the job after the commit rather than before it? What could be lost in this design, and how does the Outbox pattern solve it?
Why do we pass only a `Guid` to the job? What happens if you pass the full entity and it changes before execution?
Why is checking the extension or `ContentType` insufficient? What are the leading bytes of JPEG, PNG, and WebP files?
What happens if `mark-succeeded` arrives at the exact same moment JOB-03 executes? How do you prevent the race condition?
Why did you choose basic auth for the Hangfire dashboard? And why doesn't JWT work here?
What is the difference between Fire-and-forget, Delayed, and Recurring jobs? And why does `AddOrUpdate` not duplicate the job on every restart?
What is the difference between `$"Donation {id}"` and `"Donation {DonationId}"` in Serilog?
How do you find all the logs for a single request that failed for a user?
Why are receipts stored outside `wwwroot` while banners are public?
Why does the date appear in Hijri if you use the `ar` culture?

solutionBlocks.markdown: **NTF-07 (Welcome email):** The exact same pattern — after `CreateAsync` succeeds for the user, call `jobs.EnqueueWelcomeEmail(user.Id)`, and the job loads the user and their language and sends the email. For idempotency, add `WelcomeEmailSentAt` to `ApplicationUser`.

**NTF-08 (Campaign expired without reaching its goal):** Inside `ExpireCampaignsJob`, collect the IDs of campaigns expired in the batch, and after a successful `SaveChangesAsync`, enqueue an email job for each one (using an `ExpiredEmailSentAt` marker).
**Seq sink:** Run Seq locally, add the `Serilog.Sinks.Seq` package, and add a new sink in configuration:

First-run environment variables in the `datalust/seq` image have changed across versions (authentication is enabled by default in recent releases). Check the image documentation if the container refuses to start.

**FIL-08 (CSV export):** An Admin query builds the file with `StringBuilder` and returns `File(bytes, "text/csv", "donations.csv")`. Watch out for **CSV injection**: any value starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@` is prefixed with `'`:

**JOB-06 (Daily summary to Admin):** A second recurring job using the same approach: `AddOrUpdate<DailySummaryJob>("daily-admin-summary", j => j.RunAsync(CancellationToken.None), Cron.Daily(6))` — aggregates donations from the last 24 hours and emails them. **DON-11:** In `ReceiptData`, pass `"Anonymous Donor"` (or its Arabic equivalent) instead of the donor's name when `IsAnonymous = true`. **FIL-09:** If you use an image-processing library, verify that its license suits your project before adding it.

If your solution upholds these same **principles** — a fast HTTP request that never waits on PDF or SMTP, jobs enqueued after commit that accept IDs only and tolerate running twice, files validated by content and stored under random names, a protected dashboard with secrets kept out of Git, and structured logs searchable by `traceId` — then you are on the right track even if implementation details differ.
